records.title: Metabase CVE-2026-72898: an unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day gave attackers administrator access to BI instances, exploited since at least 3 August, with VenariX counting fifteen downstream victims
records.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded
records.summary: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally were the first to confirm customer data was taken, on 2026-08-03. The flaw went a week without a CVE identifier before it was assigned CVE-2026-72898 and added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.
actions: Upgrade every self-hosted Metabase to at least 0.58.24 / 0.59.21 / 0.60.17 / 0.61.11 / 0.62.9 / 0.63.5, then, for any instance that was reachable and unpatched during the exploitation window, revoke all active sessions by clearing the core_session table, delete unrecognised API keys, and rotate the credentials for every connected database and warehouse, not just the Metabase admin credentials, because the upgrade does not invalidate what was already retrieved.

Search Metabase application or reverse-proxy ingress logs across the entire pre-upgrade exposure window for a POST to /api/session/reset_password returning HTTP 400 immediately followed by a GET to /api/user/current returning HTTP 200 from the same source; Metabase states that sequence indicates the instance was likely compromised.

last_development.summary: Huntress's update of 2026-10-19 reports a second tenant with scripted post-compromise activity (the application granting itself Global Administrator and planting a secret on other applications, the choice of applications apparently random), bounds the sign-in activity to the morning of 2026-10-15 UTC with the last successful sign-in at 08:44 UTC, and says Graph directory reads leave no audit record; the secret check therefore has to cover every application.

records.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick): the vendor's Microsoft 365 application credential was used to sign in to customer tenants, with directory-role self-assignments in about 50 tenants and, Huntress reports, added credentials in two
records.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
records.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. How the credential was obtained, who is behind it and what data was read are not public.
actions: In every Entra tenant you or your MSP administer, disable without deleting the seven ConnectWise application identities that ConnectWise lists by client ID (Cloud Backup is 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; the other six are in ConnectWise's advisory), dormant connections included, and keep them disabled until ConnectWise gives restoration instructions; where Graph activity logs were enabled, review them for these apps until at least 90 minutes after you disabled them, because a token issued before the disable stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and preserve the sign-in and audit logs promptly without delaying containment, because Entra ID Free keeps only 7 days.
In the same tenants list the apps owned by the ConnectWise S-K LLC tenant (3f9cd7a0-127a-4ed4-bf06-2f830d5616b7), and disable each that you do not use or cannot verify as safe.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.

records.title: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating
records.headline: PK Softech: Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB of federal pension data and demands ransom; unconfirmed
records.summary: The Confederation, in a release headlined "data outflow confirmed", said on 2026-10-08 that a software supplier of Publica detected a cyberattack at the end of September, and the supplier PK Softech AG (Reinach BL) says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT infrastructure and that it must be assumed data left its systems; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Publica insures, among others, staff of the federal administration and the ETH domain, about 70,000 active members and 41,600 pensioners at the end of 2025, and says personal data of insured persons has presumably left, while the AWP agency relays the supplier's position that the volume is rather small and the data may be business data. Blick reports, citing a confidential federal information note, that the Confederation rates the incident as serious and that the security organs of the Confederation are particularly affected, which Blick glosses as the Federal Intelligence Service, the Defence Group and fedpol. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich now says personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch to its system, was stolen, and Pensionskasse Post says personal data did leave but not yet whether its insured persons' data is among it; the Bernische Pensionskasse now says, contrary to the supplier's earlier information, that it must be assumed personal data left, the pension consultancy Libera AG says it is also affected without knowing whose data, and the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse is still checking. Which fields were taken is still being clarified by each fund and the access vector is not public; Tamedia reports, and Inside IT relays, that the Akira ransomware group holds about 100 GB of the data of well over 100,000 current and former federal employees, including staff of the security authorities, and demands ransom, which neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked salary and pension data for investment-fraud calls, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK, a customer since 2011, says it runs the software in its own data centre and is not directly affected.
actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment and what it holds.

records.title: CVE-2026-0257, Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect: pre-auth authentication bypass via certificate reuse, marked by CISA as used in ransomware campaigns
records.headline: Qilin and Inc ransomware exploit the GlobalProtect bypass; one intrusion pivoted to vCenter and ESXi past in-guest EDR
records.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.
actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed release in Palo Alto's advisory for its train, or disable authentication override cookies or give them a certificate that no other service uses, then force one re-authentication so override cookies regenerate.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs), and extend the assessment to the virtualization and backup tier: vCenter and ESXi audit logs for a changed execInstalledOnly setting and for access to a domain controller's virtual disk, and the Veeam backup server, because Unit 42 describes one intrusion that pivoted from the gateway to vCenter and dumped domain credentials offline, which in-guest EDR does not see.

records.title: TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix
records.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
records.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 UTC, and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the vendor's fix and the discoverer's reading of it disagree on which keys the update removes.
actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with UpdraftPlus, free or premium, including old municipal, campaign and project sites, check for an UpdraftCentral key (wp option get updraft_central_localkeys, or Settings > UpdraftPlus Backups > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral) and delete every key even if nobody remembers using UpdraftCentral, then update to 1.26.13 or 2.26.13 or later; deleting a key stops remote management only, and backups keep working.

On any site where a plugin, must-use plugin or Editor account holding manage_options appears that nobody created, delete the UpdraftCentral key first, then restore the site from a backup taken before 17 October, rotate every administrator and UpdraftCentral password and end all sessions.

records.title: APT28 (Swallowtail) used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and an aircraft-engine maker in two NATO states; at the shipbuilder it then pushed an SSH key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes and ran a reflective loader
records.headline: Symantec: APT28's hidden-Edge backdoor hit law-enforcement and defence targets; at a shipbuilder it added an SSH tunnel
records.summary: Symantec reports that APT28, which it tracks as Swallowtail, used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft-engine manufacturer in two NATO member states, none named. A macro-enabled Word document started a script chain that uses a hidden, off-screen Microsoft Edge window as its HTTP client against a public webhook service; at the shipbuilder the operators then pushed an SSH private key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes from the host itself and ran a previously undocumented in-memory loader, in an intrusion that lasted at least two months. Recorded Future had documented HOOKEDGE against government and diplomatic targets in Romania, Spain and Turkiye in August.

records.title: eMudhra: the private keys of eight intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates; browsers block them, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go)
records.headline: Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; browsers are protected, Go, Python, Rust and curl stacks need updates
records.summary: On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms now block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them, but software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated; Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, and Chrome removes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root on 2026-10-27. No exploitation is reported.
actions: Update the trust store or toolchain of every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation (Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, Python certifi 2026.10.19, rustls-webpki 0.103.16, webpki-roots 1.0.10, the curl CA bundle of 2026-10-20, the distribution ca-certificates package, container base images) and rebuild images that embed an older bundle, then confirm with curl against the tracker's test host that the client now rejects the certificate; replace before 2026-10-27 every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3.

records.title: AA26-293A: FBI, CISA and German and UK law enforcement describe SafePay ransomware, which enters through VPN credentials and five edge-device and backup-server flaws and factory-resets backup NAS devices before encrypting
records.headline: Joint advisory on SafePay: VPN credentials and five old edge and backup flaws in, backup NAS wiped before encryption
records.summary: CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service, Germany's LKA Rheinland-Pfalz and UK law enforcement published advisory AA26-293A on 2026-10-20 on SafePay, which they say was among the most active ransomware groups in 2026 and has affected at least 600 victims, in Europe among other regions. Access comes from exposed credentials, brute force and phished account profiles used over Mullvad VPN addresses, and from five known flaws in Cisco ASA and Firepower Threat Defense, Veeam Backup and Replication and SonicWall SonicOS; the distinctive step is stopping the Volume Shadow Copy Service and factory-resetting the network storage that holds backups before encryption.

records.title: Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update: six unauthenticated network CVSS 10.0 rows in Access Manager, SOA Suite, E-Business Suite and JD Edwards, and WebLogic CVSS 9.8 flaws reachable over HTTP and T3/IIOP
records.headline: Oracle's October CPU carries six unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 rows and two WebLogic 9.8 flaws; none is reported exploited
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Patch Update of 2026-10-20 carries 1295 new patches. Its risk matrices list 90 rows (73 distinct CVE ids) scored CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher that need no authentication over the network, among them six at 10.0 in Access Manager, SOA Suite (three), E-Business Suite Workflow Notification Mailer and JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Orchestrator, and two WebLogic Server flaws at 9.8 reachable over HTTP and over T3 and IIOP. The advisory states no exploitation for any row, and it points to My Oracle Support documents for patch availability.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP: two critical flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, which CERT-EU reads as possible remote code execution, are to be fixed in a release pre-announced for 21 October 14:00 UTC, with a screenshot of an exploit tool reported leaked
records.headline: PHP announces a critical security release for 14:00 UTC on 21 October; an exploit tool screenshot is reported leaked
records.summary: The PHP security team announced on 2026-10-20 a security release for Wednesday 2026-10-21 at 14:00 UTC that fixes two critical flaws, both CVSS 4.0 9.2, and may ship earlier if details leak or exploitation starts. CERT-EU names them CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and reads them as potential unauthenticated remote code execution, and Sansec reports a leaked screenshot of an exploit tool and expects mass attacks within 15 minutes of the release. The fix goes into the PHP runtime on the host or in the container image, not into any CMS or plugin, and PHP 8.1 and older are outside upstream support.
actions: Before 14:00 UTC on 2026-10-21 list every internet-facing host and container image that runs PHP with its version (php -v) and its owner, find those on PHP 8.1 or older, and agree who restarts PHP-FPM or the web server once the fixed build is published; ask each hosting provider and distribution for its date, because OS packages, control panels and container images may follow a different schedule from php.net.

records.title: actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action compromised in Mini Shai-Hulud: 53 tags moved to imposter commits that read Runner.Worker memory, re-enabled in September with the tags intact
records.headline: The compromised actions-cool GitHub Actions were re-enabled in September with malicious tags and ran the payload again
records.summary: On 2026-05-18 all 53 version tags of the actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action, and all 15 of actions-cool/maintain-one-comment, were moved to imposter commits whose payload reads the Runner.Worker process memory for decrypted workflow secrets and sends them over HTTPS to an attacker-controlled domain (StepSecurity); Socket places the compromise in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. GitHub disabled both repositories on 2026-05-19 but they became reachable again on 2026-09-16 with the malicious tags intact, so tag-referencing workflows ran the payload again and SafeDep counted six newly infected repositories by 2026-09-24, until GitHub disabled both again by 2026-09-25 (Socket, The Hacker News). Only workflows pinned to a full commit SHA from before 2026-05-18 were unaffected.
actions: Find every workflow in your GitHub organisations that references actions-cool/issues-helper or actions-cool/maintain-one-comment by tag; where either ran successfully on 2026-05-18 to 05-19 or 2026-09-16 to 09-25, rotate every secret that workflow could read and check the repository's commits since 2026-09-16 for added Claude Code or VS Code hook files, then remove the action or pin it to a full commit SHA from before 2026-05-18.

records.title: GhostAction returns: stolen maintainer credentials push a fake security-audit workflow into the victims' own GitHub repositories, which now harvests credentials from the entire git history
records.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
records.summary: StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. GitGuardian's own data puts the wave of 8 to 12 October at more than 30,000 repositories reached through about 1,900 compromised GitHub accounts, and says GitHub has prevented the workflow from running since 9 October; no malicious package release from the stolen credentials had been seen as of 2026-10-09.
actions: Run an organisation-scoped GitHub code search in every organisation your teams and suppliers administer for workflow files under .github/workflows that present themselves as a security audit, a security check or an Actions security workflow and were added since 2026-08-31; any hit means assume breach: revoke the credential that committed it and rotate every secret found anywhere in the repository's git history, not only the configured Actions secrets.

records.title: CVE-2026-102489 / CVE-2026-102490, Zammad helpdesk: a session-hijack remote code execution and a zammad-to-root escalation, both reported exploited since 21 September; 7.2.2 fixes the root flaw on DEB and RPM installs
records.headline: Zammad 6.5.5 is an emergency fix for the exploited session-leak RCE on 6.5; 7.2.2 fixes the root escalation
records.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.
actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.2 (7.2.0 is affected by the 27 advisories Zammad published on 2026-10-06); a 6.5 instance that cannot be upgraded yet gets the 6.5.5 emergency fix from Zammad's new 6.5 package repository, and an older instance that cannot be upgraded goes offline.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised.

records.title: CVE-2026-15176 / CVE-2026-93479 / CVE-2026-97205, NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus: three unauthenticated heap-corruption flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, reachable only in specific configurations and fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7
records.headline: Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7; Debian stable is not yet
records.summary: The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian's bookworm and trixie packages are still marked vulnerable.
actions: Run nginx -T on every internet-facing NGINX reverse proxy, load balancer and ingress and upgrade each one whose configuration uses alias with rewrite and $request_filename, a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or aio together with ssi, HTTP/3 or TLS session ticket key rotation to nginx 1.30.6 or 1.31.7 (NGINX Plus 37.0.5.1 or 37.1.0.1); where the package comes from Debian bookworm or trixie, which the tracker still marks vulnerable, apply F5's configuration workaround until the distribution ships a fix.

last_update.summary: ENISA's EUVD record for CVE-2026-21589, which carried the rejection sentence from 2026-10-16, was updated on 2026-10-19 and again carries the full vulnerability description and the fixed versions; exploitation since 2026-10-15 is still listed and Atlassian's advisory is unchanged. Tooling keyed on the ID may have dropped the flaw while the record was rejected and should be re-run.

last_development.summary: Atlassian, the assigner, rejected the CVE record for CVE-2026-21589 on 2026-10-16, giving only the generic reason that its publication may have been a false positive or a mistake; ENISA's EUVD record mirrors it and still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15. Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID with the same fixed versions, and no source says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.

records.title: CVE-2026-21589, Atlassian Data Center: unauthenticated arbitrary file access in every version of eight self-managed products, patch or take them off the internet (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record, rejected on 16 October, reads as restored in ENISA's database; the flaw and its exploitation stand
records.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, without saying what the evidence is. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application. The record for this ID was marked rejected on 2026-10-16 with only a generic reason and ENISA's database shows it restored with its full description on 2026-10-19, while Atlassian's advisory and fixed versions read unchanged, so tooling keyed on the ID may have dropped the flaw in between.
actions: Upgrade every Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center installation to a fixed version of its line (Bitbucket 9.4.26, 10.2.8 or 10.5.1; Confluence 9.2.26 or 10.2.19; Jira Service Management 5.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Jira Software 9.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Bamboo 10.2.24 or 12.1.12; Crowd 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7 or 7.2.4) and Crucible and Fisheye to 4.9.15, internet-reachable instances first; until each is upgraded, take it off the internet or put Atlassian's web application firewall or Tomcat rewrite rule in front of it.

On every Jira instance that was internet-reachable and unpatched and is integrated with Crowd, treat the Crowd application password in its WEB-INF/classes/crowd.properties as readable: rotate it after the upgrade and review Crowd for user accounts created or group memberships changed since the exposure began; on every affected instance search the web server and proxy logs back to 2026-10-05, the day the advisory published (honeypots recorded the first attempts on 2026-10-06), for '..' next to '/', '\\' or '::'.

Confirm that every vulnerability scanner, SIEM enrichment rule and ticket keyed on CVE-2026-21589 reports each affected Atlassian instance as open again; where a feed dropped the ID while the record was rejected between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-19, re-run it so no exploited instance stays reported as closed.

records.title: CVE-2026-88779, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: a SAML-triggered memory overflow still hits appliances on the September fixed builds, and Citrix confirms targeted attacks (CVSS 4.0 8.7)
records.headline: Citrix confirms attacks on a new NetScaler SAML flaw that the September fixed builds do not close
records.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 fixes CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that a network attacker needing no privileges reaches when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider; Citrix says it has observed targeted attacks and scopes the impact to denial of service. Appliances already on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds that fixed the September zero-days remain affected and must move to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds, and identity-provider appliances then need 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds, which close the further SAML flaw CVE-2026-107406 that Citrix disclosed on 2026-10-08. Reports of code execution on patched honeypots are unconfirmed, and CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 2026-10-04. Rapid7's incident analysis of 2026-10-19 shows the crash used as the reboot trigger of a root-execution chain with CVE-2026-88771 on an affected 14.1 appliance, so repeated crashes on an appliance not yet patched for that flaw call for a compromise check.
actions: Upgrade every SAML-configured NetScaler (`add authentication samlAction` or `add authentication samlIdPProfile`) that is still below 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28, 14.1-73.41 FIPS or 13.1-37.282, including appliances on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds, to at least those builds; identity providers then need the builds named for CVE-2026-107406. Where the upgrade has to wait and NetScaler Console virtual patching is available, confirm with `show appfw signatures` that the Global Deny List signature version is at least v24, which Citrix offers as a bridge for CVE-2026-88779 only.

Before restarting a SAML-configured NetScaler that has crashed or rebooted repeatedly, preserve its logs and crash artifacts, open a Citrix support case, which Citrix asks for when an appliance is experiencing the impact, and search its authentication logs for shell metacharacters next to Pitboss crash-message text, because Rapid7 saw a crash-and-reboot cycle used to make the call-home crash handler run an attacker's payload as root.

records.title: CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: unauthenticated pre-auth RCE zero-days exploited before a patch existed (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Two exploited NetScaler zero-days: one in default configuration, one on by default on VPN servers; no workaround
records.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.
actions: Upgrade every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.37+ (14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.37 FIPS+) or 13.1-64.23+ (13.1-FIPS/NDcPP 13.1-37.279+) now (a SAML-configured appliance needs the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779, and an identity provider 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29); on a 13.1-branch appliance run `show ns variable` first; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop. Capture logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle and a core dump from each exposed appliance BEFORE patching, since the upgrade can remove forensic evidence of prior exploitation.

Run Mandiant's compromise checks, extended by the Unit 42 artifacts described in the update below, Zscaler's (appliance-initiated downloads to unfamiliar addresses, an unexpected executable under /var, a Perl CGI handler added to the web server configuration) and Rapid7's (the setuid bit on /bin/sh, nsaaad crashes followed by Pitboss reboots, an outbound agent polling an external endpoint every 15 seconds), on every NetScaler that was internet-facing and unpatched at any time since early September, patched or not; isolate any hit, check both nodes of an HA pair, halt HA configuration sync until both nodes are validated, and rotate the LDAP and RADIUS bind credentials, SSL private keys and key-encryption material held in the configuration, since Rapid7 saw the configuration and backups staged and exfiltrated.

Find any NetScaler ADC or Gateway still on the end-of-life 12.1 or 13.0 branches and decide isolation or replacement now: they receive no security updates and Citrix has not said whether they are affected.

records.title: BACS publishes five security classes for authentication methods: static secrets should in principle no longer be used, and only session-bound methods resist real-time phishing
records.headline: BACS grades logins in five classes: static secrets should in principle go; session binding resists phishing
records.summary: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) published on 2026-10-19 a technology assessment that sorts authentication methods, tokens and services into the classes tief, mittel and hoch, with a star on mittel and hoch for resistance to real-time phishing. It says methods in class tief, those built on a secret that is the same at every login, should in principle no longer be used. The classification is non-binding and gives no basis for testing or certification; it is a rough guideline from the federal authority for writing authentication requirements.

records.title: OVHcloud CLI: release binaries of already-published versions were replaced on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, uploaded through a developer's GitHub account
records.headline: OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it
records.summary: OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build meant to collect secrets from the disk; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched; OpenSourceMalware has not analysed the payload and OVHcloud says it is still examining the binary.
actions: Find every workstation, build agent and container image build that installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI from a release asset (install script, Homebrew cask, direct download or a CI step fetching the release tarball) between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on 2026-10-19, and rotate every secret readable on each of those hosts before installing v0.16.0 or later.

records.title: CVE-2026-110936, Siemens Software Center: a ClickFix campaign runs a genuine signed copy of the application and side-loads its own DLLs, and Siemens confirms exploitation (CVSS 4.0 8.4)
records.headline: Siemens confirms exploitation of a Software Center DLL side-loading flaw; attackers bring their own signed copy
records.summary: Siemens ProductCERT says it validated active exploitation of CVE-2026-110936, a DLL side-loading flaw in Siemens Software Center versions before V4.0.9.8, which it fixed in advisory SSA-580366 of 2026-10-15; installed copies update themselves the next time the application starts. The attackers did not abuse an installed copy: they delivered a genuine, validly signed copy of version 3.5.8.7 with their own files beside it through what Siemens calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign, so the check that finds it is behaviour on any Windows PC, not a Software Center inventory.

records.title: Phishing lures sent as ICS calendar invites land in Outlook and Gmail calendars without a click and stay after the email is deleted; EvilTokens used them for Microsoft 365 device-code phishing
records.headline: Calendar-invite phishing spreads: Outlook and Gmail add the lure on their own and keep it after the email is deleted
records.summary: Netcraft reports that phishing lures delivered as ICS calendar files, adopted by widespread campaigns of the EvilTokens Microsoft 365 token-stealing kit, are now spreading to low-effort scams. Outlook with Exchange Online (desktop, web and mobile) and Gmail with Google Calendar add such an invite to the calendar automatically as tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, so purging the message leaves the lure in place. EvilTokens invites posed as meetings, alerts or voicemail and led to a device-code page that has the victim authorise an attacker's device through OAuth; Sublime Security, quoted by The Guardian, reports exponential growth in calendar phishing.

last_update.summary: Corrects four statements: PaperCut says only that Emergency Patch Release 3 addresses two known regressions, not that Release 2 introduced them (the record of 2026-09-03 says it did); the web-log hunt now covers the LogonMessage route watchTowr documents and is cited; Huntress's 47% figure is dated to 28 August; and GreyNoise's twelve domain-admin victims are its count at last observation, not a final tally out of 395. The attacker-chosen Derby database name is removed from the detection text and the action as an indicator value.

last_development.summary: Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.

records.title: CVE-2026-82078 / CVE-2026-81578, PaperCut NG/MF: an Apache Tapestry request-routing confusion chains an unauthenticated config rewrite to arbitrary code execution, exploited before a patch existed
records.headline: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
records.summary: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain, CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4), that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. Fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 (10 September 2026) replace the emergency patches and are the vendor's recommended build (the September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now names 24.1.11 for v24); servers still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2 need to upgrade now. There is no fix for v23 and earlier, and Huntress estimated on 28 August that 47% of the PaperCut installs it tracks ran v23 or older. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10. Hunt.io's recovery of the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) adds a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API, usable when its address allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, and live pivots into 45 victims, with Switzerland among the countries listed.
actions: Upgrade every PaperCut NG/MF Application Server, Site Server and secondary/print server to the security maintenance release for its line (26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.11, the v24 build the September bulletin now names), starting with any still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2, because the emergency builds do not carry the fix for CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor's September bulletin lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10; for v23 and earlier, immediately restrict the Application Server's web interface to trusted/internal IP addresses only; no patch exists for that line. On every server, patched or not, set the advanced config key auth.webservices.auth-token to a long random secret and limit auth.webservices.allowed-addresses to the hosts that call the XML-RPC API, because Hunt.io says an instance hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against the XML-RPC route it recovered, which works when the allowlist is too permissive or no token is set.

Before patching or restarting an internet-facing server, preserve the server/logs directory and process tree; check server.log for the two vendor-documented error strings and for an unexplained gap or truncation, check server.log and derby.log for an in-memory Derby database booted under an attacker-chosen name, and hunt for a Windows service named "Remote Access Service" running SimpleService.exe (SimpleHelp) or an unexpected AnyDesk install, as PaperCut's own published incident data names both as an observed post-compromise access method.

Given GreyNoise's confirmed domain-admin escalation paths, verify no PaperCut Application Server is domain-joined with a privileged service account or hosted on a domain controller, and confirm domain controllers reachable from any PaperCut host are patched against the 2021 noPac flaws (CVE-2021-42278/CVE-2021-42287); GreyNoise reports the AI-orchestrated campaign reaching full domain admin through these paths in as little as five minutes after initial access.

records.title: Claroty Team82: 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory refrigeration controllers chain to unauthenticated root RCE — a deterministic admin password derived from the device's own MAC address is one of THREE independent pre-auth paths
records.headline: An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal
records.summary: Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 18 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws score CVSS 8.0 each, and CISA's advisory adds two low-severity unauthenticated flaws. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.
actions: Upgrade every Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO controller to firmware v1.13 now, and treat any internet-exposed unit as a compromise-assessment candidate regardless of prior authentication controls: the deterministic-password path is fully reconstructable offline from data available at unauthenticated public endpoints, so a strong admin password alone did not protect an unpatched device.

records.title: Rank Math SEO PRO 3.0.123: some packages served for about eleven hours carried malware that can leave hidden backdoors, rogue administrators and cron persistence that the update to 3.0.124 does not remove
records.headline: Some Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 downloads carried malware; updating to 3.0.124 does not remove what it left
records.summary: Rank Math says some copies of its WordPress plugin Rank Math PRO 3.0.123, downloaded or updated between 2026-10-15 20:02 UTC and 2026-10-16 07:12 UTC, contained malware that could compromise a site once the plugin is activated, and it released 3.0.124 as the clean build. The malware can recreate a hidden backdoor on page visits and may leave administrator accounts, scheduled tasks and files outside the plugin, so an affected site needs the plugin folder and persistence removed in a set order, a restore or cleanup, and rotation of every credential the site could reach; how the vendor's distribution was compromised and who is behind it are not disclosed.
actions: Find every WordPress site that your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with Rank Math PRO and establish whether 3.0.123 was downloaded or updated between 2026-10-15 20:02 UTC and 2026-10-16 07:12 UTC; on a site where it was activated, restore from a backup older than that window or, if cleaning by hand, delete the whole rank-math-pro folder and the malicious database options first, because the backdoor is rebuilt on page visits, and rotate every credential the site could reach.

records.title: CVE-2026-85097, Bricksforge for WordPress: an unauthenticated upload in the Pro Forms module writes attacker PHP into the uploads directory, exploited since 7 October; fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0, with a related upload fix in 4.0.1 (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Bricksforge's Pro Forms upload flaw is exploited without login since 7 October; fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0, related fix in 4.0.1
records.summary: Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's revised changelog states the flaw was fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0 and lists a related Pro Forms upload fix in 4.0.1 of 2026-10-08; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry.
actions: Find every WordPress site that your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with Bricksforge and update it to version 4.0.1 or later (at least 3.1.8.10 on the 3.x line) now, treating any site that was reachable and unpatched since 2026-10-07 as one to search for dropped PHP files.

last_development.summary: CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost reported at hundreds of French supermarkets; CERT-FR and NCSC Switzerland say to remove internet exposure
records.headline: CERT-FR adds Copeland and Dixell xweb to the hijacked refrigeration controllers; NCSC.ch rates the attacks exploited
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware; no source names an actor, the flaw or how the attackers got in, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, against the intended one; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and change the default passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

records.title: CVE-2026-84411, MikroTik RouterOS: one unauthenticated request to the web management service can run code as root; fixed in 7.24 (v7 stable), 7.23.8 (v7 long-term) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term) (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: MikroTik's long-term changelogs already carry the fix for a pre-auth RouterOS RCE; its notice still says pending
records.summary: MikroTik's notice of 2026-10-06 describes CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request body handling of the RouterOS web management service (WebFig, on the www and www-ssl ports) that one crafted request sent without logging in can use to crash the service or run code on the router with full privileges; CISA scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. RouterOS before 7.24, v6 included, is affected where an attacker can reach the web interface; 7.24 fixes the v7 stable channel and MikroTik's changelogs list the fix in 7.23.8 (v7 long-term, 2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term, 2026-10-07), although its notice still shows both long-term releases as pending; MikroTik says the default firewall already blocks the web interface from the internet, and CISA records no known public exploitation.
actions: Find every RouterOS device whose www or www-ssl service answers from a network you do not trust and upgrade it to the fixed build for its channel: 7.24 or later on v7 stable, 7.23.8 on v7 long-term, 6.49.23 on v6 long-term; where an upgrade has to wait, restrict www and www-ssl under IP > Services to trusted addresses or disable them and manage the router over WinBox, SSH or a VPN.

records.title: CVE-2026-102255, SonicWall SMA1000: a third unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Work Place SSRF this year, affecting the hotfix builds that closed the September zero-days, with exploitation attempts reported that SonicWall has not confirmed
records.headline: NCSC.ch now rates the SonicWall SMA1000 pre-auth SSRF actively exploited; SonicWall still reports no evidence
records.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 (2026-10-06) fixes four SMA1000 flaws, led by CVE-2026-102255, a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the Work Place interface (CVSS 3.0 10.0) that affects 12.4.3-03526 and 12.5.0-02952, the hotfixes issued for the September zero-days; fixed builds are 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082. Two honeypot operators report exploitation attempts against the flaw, Defused from 2026-10-08 and Previdian from 2026-10-09, and NCSC Switzerland recorded it as actively exploited on 2026-10-12, without anyone establishing that an attempt would have compromised a system; SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation. The two earlier unauthenticated Work Place SSRF flaws this year were exploited, each paired with an administrator-only command-execution flaw.
actions: Install SonicWall's platform hotfix 12.4.3-03670 or 12.5.0-03082 (or higher) on every SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v, internet-reachable appliances first and including appliances already on the 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 hotfix from September; the appliance restarts when the installation finishes and no workaround is listed.

On every SMA1000 whose Work Place interface was internet-reachable before the hotfix, check its web access log back to 2026-10-06, the day the advisory was published, for the requests Previdian describes and, on a hit, run the compromise check SonicWall's earlier guidance describes.

records.title: CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134, AhsayCBS backup management console: an unauthenticated authentication-bypass and code-execution chain exploited since 7 October to drop webshells and a cryptominer; Ahsay says its earlier patches were incomplete and ships hotfixes 10.3.4.45 and 9.15.2.70 through its partner portal
records.headline: Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.
actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run, including those already on v10.3.4.0 or v9.15.2.59, and apply the hotfix v10.3.4.45 (v10) or v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8, v9) now, then reboot it; the hotfixes sit behind Ahsay's partner portal, so ask the integrator or Ahsay for the build, and until it is applied keep the management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses.

Compromise-check every AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04 against the indicators Huntress and Bitdefender publish, an OpenSSH service nobody installed included, and against Horizon3's server-side checks (new .jsp files in served application directories, replication receivers created outside a change window, unexpected system administrator accounts), and re-image any host with a confirmed compromise from a trusted backup, because the hotfix does not remove a webshell or a persistence mechanism that is already there.

records.title: CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)
records.headline: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 Exchange security updates fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow that an unauthenticated attacker can trigger with a crafted email (Critical, CVSS 8.1 with high attack complexity, Exploitation More Likely, not exploited), and CVE-2026-70279, a 9.3 cross-site scripting flaw that lets an attacker act as an administrator who clicks a crafted link. October is the last month Exchange 2016 and 2019 customers enrolled in the Period 2 ESU receive newly released updates, and organisations without ESU have no 2016 or 2019 update at all. Microsoft's Exchange Team says the October Windows Server updates (KB5126646, KB5126655, KB5126651, KB5126868) can make Exchange servers unstable, with OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum, whether or not the Exchange update is installed; it advises against uninstalling them and on 2026-10-17 gave a registry workaround.
actions: Install the October 2026 Exchange security update on every Exchange server and on every machine that has the Exchange Management Tools; on Exchange 2016 and 2019 servers that are not covered by the Period 2 ESU, decide now between enrolling (it only gets an organisation current through this release) and moving to Exchange Subscription Edition, because after October Microsoft ships updates for Subscription Edition only.

On every Exchange server that has the October 2026 Windows Server update installed, do not uninstall it; where OWA fails with MapiExceptionMdbOffline, mail queues grow or a DAG member cannot reach quorum, set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Rpc to 65536, reboot, and raise the limit if the failure recurs.

last_development.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. records.title: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, and the root-escalation step of the chain was unpatched at disclosure (CVSS 8.6)
records.headline: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker
records.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti had not fixed when Volexity reported (a separate record, CVE-2026-111357, now covers that step), patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5 (Rapid7 also lists 25.1.3.0, which CERT-FR counts as affected); a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.
actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on 25.1.1.1 or earlier, 25.1.2.2 or earlier, or 22.8R2.4 or earlier to 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.5 now, internet-facing appliances first; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.

records.title: AOMEI Backupper and AnyViewer update files tampered with for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026 to push the CROSSROAD downloader and the SHINYROAD backdoor, with Switzerland among 11 countries GTIG names
records.headline: GTIG: AOMEI update files were altered for minutes at a time to push a backdoor; Switzerland among victim countries
records.summary: Google's GTIG and ManageEngine's METAL report that a cluster tracked as UNC7017 altered two configuration files on AOMEI's update servers for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026, so any Backupper or AnyViewer client that polled during a window downloaded and ran the CROSSROAD downloader, which installed the SHINYROAD backdoor beside a signed Radmin binary. No software flaw is involved, GTIG names Switzerland among 11 victim countries, and the vendor's server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader, so installations need an endpoint hunt covering April to July 2026.
actions: Inventory every Windows host that runs AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer and check each for scheduled tasks named RadminComponentRuntime or NitroRuntime, a Radmin directory under the user's local application data and cached update files in the install tree's Tmphtml folder, searching proxy and firewall logs back to April 2026; isolate any host that matches and keep the cached files before any cleanup.

last_update.summary: CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-16, after this entry was published; the CVE record and tags now carry the listing. The entry already described the flaw as exploited.

records.title: PEERSTITCH: a memory-resident FortiGate implant installed through the FortiOS CLI path traversal CVE-2025-61624, which Fortinet lists as exploited and leaves unfixed on FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, after a FortiManager compromise exposed the configurations of 500+ firewalls
records.headline: Unit 42: a memory-resident FortiGate implant rides an exploited FortiOS flaw that has no fix on 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4
records.summary: Unit 42 describes a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as CL-STA-0954 (UNC5820), that began with the FortiManager flaw CVE-2024-47575, exfiltrated the configurations and cryptographic material of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and later used the FortiOS CLI auto-script path traversal CVE-2025-61624 to install PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 implant that patches the logging and IPsec daemons in memory and leaves no persistent binary on disk. Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 lists CVE-2025-61624 as known exploited and gives no fix for FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, only a move to a fixed release, so those branches stay exposed to an attacker who already holds a privileged administrator account.

records.title: CL-UNK-1211: an AI-assisted intrusion set against government Linux web and mail servers persists through PHP auto_prepend_file, steals sudo passwords with a fake prompt and reads mail stores, and tries to pass as a red-team exercise
records.headline: Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit with PHP prepend persistence, a sudo password trap and mail searches
records.summary: Unit 42 reports CL-UNK-1211, a cluster of unknown nation-state or criminal affiliation that between October 2025 and April 2026 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, focusing on Linux servers to run reconnaissance and keep persistent access for intelligence collection. Its scripts carry AI-style reasoning comments, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work; the intrusions used PHP web shells with auto_prepend_file persistence on Plesk hosts, a replaced .bashrc that traps sudo passwords, SUID root shells, searches of mail directories and log cleanup. Unit 42 names no victim or country, does not say how the web shells were first placed, and is the only source.

records.title: AdFection: Citizen Lab and Confiant document zero-click Candiru spyware delivered through targeted online ads from the ad-tech firm Discover-Tech, with ad impressions on defence-ministry, armed-forces and NATO networks
records.headline: Citizen Lab: spyware delivery through targeted ads, with defence and government networks among the impressions
records.summary: Citizen Lab and Confiant report that Discover-Tech, an ad-tech firm, serves targeted ads whose code decides per device whether to return JavaScript, and that for chosen devices the chain hands off to servers Citizen Lab links with high confidence to Candiru spyware; at least 45 devices at Al Jazeera were targeted in 2024 and 2025. Citizen Lab's bidding data shows Discover-Tech ads on networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and NATO, though an impression alone does not prove infection, and neither report mentions Switzerland.

last_update.summary: Priority calibration: high moves to notable. The flaw is unexploited with no public exploit, and core alone is not directly exploitable; the known paths, including the one without login, need a contributed module or custom code, which the high bar treats as a non-default configuration.

records.title: CVE-2026-108097, Drupal core (SA-CORE-2026-014): a critical Field UI code-execution flaw reachable through contributed modules, at least one without login; fixed in 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19, with no fix for end-of-life branches (Drupal risk 19/25)
records.headline: Drupal patches a critical Field UI RCE reachable through contributed modules; uninstall field_ui if you cannot update
records.summary: Drupal's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-108097, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module rated Critical (19 of 25): core alone is not directly exploitable, but several exploit paths exist through contributed modules and at least one known path needs no login. Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below and Drupal 8 and 9 get no fix, and until a site is updated the advisory's mitigation is to uninstall the Field UI module. The advisory records no public exploit at publication, and The Hacker News relays the Security Team's pre-announcement warning that exploits might be developed within hours or days.
actions: Update every Drupal core site to 11.4.10, 11.3.19 or 10.6.19 now, internet-facing sites first, and until a site is updated uninstall its Field UI module (field_ui); update the Entity List module to 3.0.10 wherever it is installed, because updating core does not update it, and plan the migration of any site still on 11.2.x or below, 10.5.x or below, Drupal 8 or Drupal 9, which receive no fix.

last_update.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-102764 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-16, after this entry was published; the CVE record and tags now carry the listing. The entry already described the flaw as exploited.

records.title: CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: BeyondTrust patches an exploited Remote Support zero-day; the actor's persistence survives reboot and reset
records.summary: BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown.
actions: Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliance now and confirm in the /appliance interface that it is installed (a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first, which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure); apply it to self-hosted Privileged Remote Access appliances too, which BeyondTrust patched as a precaution.

For every appliance that was internet-reachable on a build up to 26.2.3 at any time since late August 2026: before any change, snapshot a virtual appliance with memory and export its disk, and collect the off-box syslog, reverse-proxy or WAF and perimeter firewall logs because the actor deletes on-appliance logs; then redeploy from a clean, fully patched image every appliance whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown, and rotate the credentials it held in dependency order, including the Remote Support Vault and any credential typed into a support session.

records.headline: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
records.summary: Adobe's 2026-10-13 bulletins fix five unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 in ColdFusion 2025 and 2023 (fixed in 2025.0.14 and 2023.0.26), three unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 code-execution flaws in Experience Manager (Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 or per-issue hotfixes) and two code-execution flaws (CVSS 10.0 and 9.8) in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (2026-oct builds). records.title: CVE-2026-0322, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS: code injection in the management interface gives an authenticated attacker root, exploited in very limited attacks and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS-B 8.6)
records.headline: Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 now published
records.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround and the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet; 11.2.16, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, was published on 2026-10-15, so every train now has a fixed build.
actions: Restrict the management interface of every PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama to a jump box or trusted internal addresses now, then upgrade each to the fixed build of its train (11.2.14 and 11.2.15 units to 11.2.16, published 2026-10-15); there is no workaround.

On every device whose management interface was reachable from untrusted networks, search management-interface logins, administrator-change records and upstream firewall logs for the three source addresses Palo Alto lists in the advisory's FAQ, and treat a match as a root compromise.

records.title: A fake WatchGuard VPN download site captures the SSL VPN server, login and password in the browser and then serves the genuine signed installer, leaving no malicious file for endpoint tools to flag
records.headline: Huntress: a lookalike VPN-client site harvests credentials, then hands over the real signed installer
records.summary: Huntress describes a lookalike WatchGuard VPN download site, reached on 2026-10-07 by an administrator at a managed service provider through a Bing search result, that asks for the SSL VPN server, login and password, rejects the first submission so the victim types again, and only then downloads the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer from WatchGuard's own CDN. No malware is delivered, so endpoint controls have no file to flag, and few reputation engines flagged the domains.

records.title: CVE-2026-110447, Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server (Nextcloud richdocumentscode app): an unauthenticated command injection in proxy.php, exploited in the wild to plant PHP web shells, fixed in 26.4.303 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it
records.summary: CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected.
actions: Update the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that runs it; disabling the app does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older, which is end of life, upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app.

On each such server, search the web access logs back to at least early September 2026 for requests to apps/richdocumentscode/proxy.php that carry $( or an encoded .. in the path, and the app directory for PHP files that are not part of the release; on a hit, treat every secret the web server account can read as exposed and rotate it.

records.title: CVE-2026-76519, Cisco Secure Email Gateway: one crafted email attachment writes files and runs commands as root, exploited in the wild and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update
records.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780.
actions: Run contentscannerstatus on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway that has File Reputation enabled in a mail policy and update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525 or later with contentscannerupdate wherever automatic updates are off; the update needs no restart.

On every such gateway, and on each member of a cluster, run grep "System Security" system_logs now: on a suspected-compromise message keep the forensic data before upgrading, then follow Cisco's recovery steps (a new virtual machine on a fixed release with a fresh configuration and renewed credentials for a virtual appliance, Cisco TAC for a physical one) for every member of that cluster.
