records.title: CVE-2026-97229, GitLab CE/EE: an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler allows code execution on self-managed servers and now has a public proof of concept; fixed in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8, and 19.4.1 does not close it (CVSS 10.0)
records.headline: GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex flaw now has a public PoC; the demonstrated path needs push access to a public project
records.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration; Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced it on 19.4.1 and published a proof of concept, and reports no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project (an ordinary account where users may create public projects), followed by a request to the CI lint API that carries no credentials. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, and NCSC Switzerland and CERT-EU both published advisories on 2026-10-12.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance on 19.2, 19.3 or 19.4 to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 now, internet-reachable instances and instances that allow open sign-up or public projects first, because a public proof of concept exists; 19.4.1 and 19.3.4 remain affected, and until each instance is upgraded, restrict anonymous access to public projects and stop untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects, which reduces exposure only to the path Rapid7 demonstrated.

records.title: Tangerhütte (Saxony-Anhalt): the vendor of the municipal citizen-portal software says attackers exploited a zero-day in it, classifies the intrusion as AI-driven, and four other communes took their portals offline
records.headline: German portal vendor reports an exploited zero-day and calls it AI-driven; police neither confirm nor deny that
records.summary: Innocon, the Tangermünde developer of the "digitales Rathaus" citizen portal, said in an MDR report of 2026-10-13 that attackers found and exploited a vulnerability it did not know of in its software, run for Tangerhütte on systems of the state municipal IT provider KID; the portal was taken offline in September and four more communes pulled theirs as a precaution. Innocon says the attackers reached only test accounts and took no real data, and classifies the intrusion as AI-driven because of command speed and on-host tool development, which is the vendor's reading: the state criminal police can neither confirm nor deny it. No CVE, product version or fix is named.

records.title: CVE-2026-96951, Windows Shell: a Mark of the Web bypass exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the 2026-10-13 cumulative updates and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.8)
records.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release.
actions: Deploy the 2026-10-13 cumulative update for each release (KB5127648 for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2, KB5127646 for Windows 11 26H1, KB5126657 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5126655 for Server 2022, KB5126646 for Server 2025, and the others listed in the CVE record) to every Windows endpoint and server, starting with the systems whose users open mail and chat attachments or download files; Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch.

The watchTowr sentence on readable files and the Triage line now say only what watchTowr says. A KEV remediation-deadline mention is dropped from the main text. records.title: CVE-2026-85706 — GitLab CE/EE: unauthenticated path traversal in the repository commits API reads arbitrary server files, and honeypots recorded probes by the day after the patch (CVSS 10.0)
records.headline: GitLab's maximum-severity file-read flaw drew in-the-wild probes by the day after its patch
records.summary: GitLab shipped 19.3.2, 19.2.6 and 19.1.8 on 2026-09-10, fixing CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0): improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement in the repository commits API let an unauthenticated user read arbitrary files from the GitLab server. Every self-managed CE/EE install from 18.7 up to those releases is affected; watchTowr's global honeypot network was recording behavioral probes for the flaw by 2026-09-11, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-09-11. GitLab backported the fix to 19.0.9 and 18.11.12 on 2026-09-23.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE/EE instance to 19.3.2 / 19.2.6 / 19.1.8 now, or on the 19.0 and 18.11 trains to the 19.0.9 / 18.11.12 backports, which carry only the CVE-2026-85706 and CVE-2026-87719 fixes and leave GitLab EE exposed to CVE-2026-88765 until 19.1.8 or later; GitLab.com is already patched and GitLab Dedicated needs no action. Assume any files an attacker-scripted request could reach (configuration files, secrets or other sensitive server-side data) may have been read, and rotate them if the instance was internet-reachable and unpatched since 2026-09-10.

records.title: NeedyMantis: Microsoft details a modular post-compromise framework, found through the DAEMON Tools compromise, used against telecoms, universities, intergovernmental bodies and government contractors
records.headline: Microsoft: a China-aligned implant hides in legitimate software via DLL sideloading and takes modules over WebSockets
records.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes NeedyMantis, a modular post-compromise malware framework used since at least October 2025 in a limited number of targeted intrusions at telecommunications organizations, universities, medical nonprofits, intergovernmental organizations and government contractors. It is deployed after access exists, sideloaded as a DLL beside legitimate software, and loads further modules over a WebSocket channel. Storm-3069, Microsoft's designator for the DAEMON Tools supply-chain activity, is one operator; Microsoft assesses Storm-3069's activity originates from China without attributing it to a nation-state actor, and has not determined whether one operator is behind all NeedyMantis activity.

last_update.summary: Zscaler describes FLATROOF payloads for macOS, Linux and Windows that drop the ROOFDECK backdoor, and identifies ROOFDECK variants only for Windows and macOS; the summary had said both families were delivered on all three platforms. The macOS detection sentence gains its SentinelLabs citation.

last_development.summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz (2026-10-08) independently reports a July 2026 trojanized Terraform provider binary that executes at plugin load and delivers FLATROOF and ROOFDECK on macOS, Linux and Windows, with Telegram, GitHub and webhook command channels and a signed Pastebin dead drop alongside the Nostr fallback; the Terraform delivery path now has a second form, and the malware family a second publisher.

records.title: TraderTraitor (Jade Sleet) backdoors resurface on a non-cryptocurrency IT-services firm in a campaign that delivers malware through weaponized Terraform provider lockfiles, resolving C2 through a Nostr-relay dead drop
records.headline: SentinelLabs: the same DPRK backdoors from a $292M crypto theft resurface on a victim with no crypto ties, in a campaign that uses poisoned Terraform lockfiles
records.summary: SentinelLabs found the FLATROOF and ROOFDECK macOS backdoors, first documented in April 2026's USD 292 million LayerZero/KelpDAO cryptocurrency theft, on an unrelated victim: a small India-based IT-services provider with no cryptocurrency ties. The campaign's fake job-interview GitHub repositories carry weaponized Terraform provider lockfiles that redirect `terraform init` to attacker-controlled provider registries, though SentinelLabs cannot prove how this victim's backdoors were delivered. Zscaler ThreatLabz independently reports a July 2026 trojanized Terraform provider binary that runs malicious code as soon as Terraform loads it and delivers FLATROOF on macOS, Linux and Windows, which drops ROOFDECK (Windows and macOS variants identified), in a campaign it suspects is TraderTraitor. The second-stage backdoor resolves its command-and-control address by reading an operator profile's public "website" field from the Nostr decentralized relay network.

last_update.summary: The Exposure line gave only S4GET's kernel scope, so a reader on an older kernel line would have concluded neither flaw applied; OVERPASS, the CVSS 10.0 flaw, affects kernel lines from 7.22 to 9.20. The headline no longer calls both flaws maximum severity (S4GET is 9.8), and the ACL sentence gains its citation.

last_development.summary: An open-source SAP exploitation toolkit, SAPMAP, publicly released on 2026-09-15, carries proof-of-concept exploits for both flaws, including OVERPASS exploits that the maintainers first said they were withholding. Onapsis had not observed attackers using it when it wrote, and no exploitation is reported. The OVERPASS routes were re-cited to Onapsis and an unsupported discriminator in the triage line was removed.

records.title: SAP September 2026 Patch Day: OVERPASS (CVE-2026-44756, CVSS 10.0) and S4GET (CVE-2026-58240, CVSS 9.8) — two unauthenticated pre-auth RCE flaws in shared SAP kernel components reachable through ports that cannot be firewalled without breaking normal SAP GUI/RFC use
records.headline: Two critical pre-auth SAP kernel flaws (CVSS 10.0 and 9.8) reach through the ports SAP GUI and RFC need; segmentation will not close them
records.summary: SAP's 8 September 2026 Patch Day fixed CVE-2026-44756 (OVERPASS, CVSS 10.0), an unauthenticated memory-corruption flaw in kernel Extended Passport processing reachable via the web tier, SAP Dispatcher or RFC, and CVE-2026-58240 (S4GET, CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated Message Server trust-bypass reachable on the port every SAP GUI client uses; both yield unauthenticated remote code execution across the SAP kernel-based product line. Neither is yet confirmed exploited, but Onapsis found over 10,000 internet-facing SAP interfaces, and since 2026-09-15 an open-source SAP exploitation toolkit, SAPMAP, has carried proof-of-concept exploits for both flaws.
actions: Apply SAP Security Notes 3747649 (OVERPASS) and 3759472 (S4GET) to every SAP kernel-based system now, internet-exposed systems first and then internal ones, because the affected components are commonly reachable through internal firewalls; public proof-of-concept exploits for both flaws have been available since 2026-09-15 in the SAPMAP toolkit, and Onapsis found over 10,000 internet-facing SAP interfaces.

last_update.summary: Elastic reads the commit-message string warning against token revocation as intimidation, and OX Security calls the same string an extortion string while describing a dead man's switch separately, which Elastic does not mention; the containment paragraph now says so. Unit 42's environment check selects a single republishing path in one project and does not gate the worm as a whole, which the earlier wording implied. The locale-gate sentence gains its citation.

last_development.summary: A further package, tensorlake@0.5.144 (the npm SDK of an AI-agent sandbox platform), was published on 2026-10-08 with a Shai-Hulud-family payload through the project's normal GitHub Actions pipeline with valid build provenance; Socket and OX Security describe the dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked, and both say to remove its persistence before revoking. Socket matches the release to this wave, while OX Security says new keys may point to an independent actor reusing the name.

records.title: CHAINDROP — the Shai-Hulud npm worm returns through the keyv maintainer, backdoors 400+ packages, and resolves its exfiltration endpoint from an Ethereum smart contract
records.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
records.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns — AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens — and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.
actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication — that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name the gh-token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.

last_update.summary: The June hunting paragraph named Windows event ids and a domain-wide rotation that no cited source gives; Fortinet's guidance is to treat directory accounts the device used as compromised and review domain controller logs. The October paragraph had attributed a FortiGate audit-log mapping to the FBI and Secret Service advisory, which names only the logs to review. The action keeps the single do-now task.

last_development.summary: A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says FortiBleed is still active: the operators create administrator accounts on compromised FortiGates and in some cases delete or change the original accounts, locking owners out, and access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. It cites SOCRadar for more than 86,644 compromised devices and adds firewall, VPN and domain controller log review, REST API key review and PBKDF2 enforcement to the response.

records.title: FortiBleed: an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls, now locking administrators out and supplying ransomware affiliates
records.headline: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds ransomware affiliates
records.summary: FortiBleed is an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with SOCRadar counting more than 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries; Fortinet said in June that it uses no new vulnerability, only reused credentials and brute force. A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says attackers keep scanning exposed devices with previously obtained credentials, create administrator accounts on compromised firewalls and in some cases delete or change the original accounts so owners are locked out, and that access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. An organisation with an internet-exposed FortiGate should end all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every credential and look for accounts and API keys it did not create.
actions: Audit every internet-facing FortiGate for administrator accounts and REST API keys nobody created, then terminate all administrator and VPN sessions and reset every administrator and VPN password.

last_update.summary: The verification value moves from single-source-victim to multi-source: the incident now rests on the authorities' own disclosure plus independent reporting by Datatilsynet and DR, and Politiken's and TV 2's reporting as relayed by Ritzau and TT, all cited in the entry.

last_development.summary: The abused company is Pays ApS of Odense, which confirmed it to TV 2; Politiken reports that at least three of its accounts, including the administrator account, used the password 123456, and an anonymous hacker says access began with a leaked former employee's password, a claim. Ritzau puts the access at 21 days and 17 hours from 10 September, where the minister had described about ten days.

records.title: Denmark's CPR population register: unauthorised parties abused a small private company's lawful lookup access, where Politiken reports at least three accounts used the password 123456, and obtained names, addresses and CPR numbers of 8.8 million people
records.headline: A Danish company's register access, reportedly secured with the password 123456, was abused to obtain 8.8 million CPR numbers
records.summary: Denmark's CPR administration says unauthorised parties used a private Danish company's lawful right to search the Central Person Register to obtain names, addresses and CPR numbers of about 8.8 million of its roughly 11 million records (living, deceased and emigrated persons); the ministry says the access does not cover the names and addresses of people with name-and-address protection. The company, Pays ApS of Odense, confirmed to TV 2 that its lawful access was abused, and Politiken reports that at least three of its accounts, including the administrator account, used the password 123456; Ritzau puts the access at 21 days and 17 hours from 10 September, where the minister had described about ten days. An anonymous hacker told Politiken the access began with a leaked former employee's password, which is the hacker's claim, and Datatilsynet describes a very large number of automated lookups made to identify valid CPR numbers.

records.title: PoeLLM: a cryptomining botnet that reads its C2 address out of a GitHub poem compromises exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers and turns them into scanners
records.headline: Lumen: a botnet takes its C2 address from a GitHub poem and spreads through exposed AI and developer servers
records.summary: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs tracks PoeLLM, a financially motivated botnet active since at least April 2026 that Lumen says has impacted more than 3,400 servers, mostly in the United States and Western Europe, among them exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers, with Ivanti Sentry possibly targeted. The malware derives its command-and-control address from words in a poem in a GitHub repository, runs XMRig and Iron miners and turns victims into scanners and exploit launchers that Lumen says likely abuse the LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 path.

records.title: Attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, rewrote authoritative DNS and obtained valid HTTPS certificates for Google and YouTube names
records.headline: Registry-level DNS hijacks of .gh, .sl and .as produced valid HTTPS certificates for Google names
records.summary: Google's Chrome team reported on 2026-10-06 that attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, changed authoritative DNS records and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains and for domains of other organizations; Chrome blocked them and Google had the issuing authorities revoke the Google certificates. Google names no attacker or entry vector and says it cannot guarantee it found every affected domain; The Hacker News found 12 certificates for Google and YouTube names in public logs, 11 issued by Let's Encrypt and one by ZeroSSL, first logged between 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-27.

records.title: ReliaQuest: LLM-driven agents run most of an intrusion through one unauthenticated Spring Batch job-submission feature on Apache Tomcat, from in-process JavaScript to SYSTEM in under 24 hours
records.headline: ReliaQuest: AI agents took a Tomcat server to SYSTEM in under a day through an exposed job-submission feature
records.summary: ReliaQuest assesses with high confidence that LLM-driven agents carried out substantial parts of an intrusion it investigated, using only known techniques: an internet-facing Apache Tomcat application accepted Spring Batch job definitions without a login, jobs ran JavaScript through the Nashorn engine inside the application process, plaintext SQL Server sysadmin credentials from the application's configuration led to xp_cmdshell, and two public privilege-escalation tools reached SYSTEM. ReliaQuest names no victim, sector or region, nor the vendor of the exposed application, and could not determine how many agents ran, which model drove them or how much a person approved.

records.title: Cisco Talos: malware now embeds natural-language instructions aimed at LLM triage pipelines, from a copied comment to template-sprayed prompts across four families, and a Russia-aligned group uses it too
records.headline: Talos: malware tells the analysing LLM to skip it; the text is plain and therefore detectable
records.summary: Cisco Talos documents 84 samples from four malware families, collected from January 2025 to July 2026, that embed plain natural-language text meant to steer the LLM stage of automated triage: a verbatim "no need to analyze this file" comment reused by at least four actors, templated variants, instructions repeated across seven chat-template formats, and intimidation or fabricated-authority text. ESET separately found UAC-0099 using a decoy request in a script comment to trip an LLM scanner's refusal; Talos' own test of five local models put the best techniques at steering the outcome in the attacker's favour in about 35% of runs, and its advice is to treat text inside a sample as evidence, never as instruction.

records.title: AA26-281A: China-linked actors enabled by Integrity Technology Group scan with MicroScan, spray Exchange and Microsoft 365 passwords and steal mail, and five old flaws from the scanner's scripts enter CISA KEV
records.headline: Joint advisory: Flax Typhoon-consistent actors spray Exchange and Microsoft 365, steal mail and keep SoftEther access
records.summary: The FBI, CISA, NSA, NCSC UK and partners from five more countries published AA26-281A on 2026-10-08 on China-linked actors enabled by Integrity Technology Group, whose tactics the advisory calls consistent with Flax Typhoon: open-source and MicroScan vulnerability scanning, XSS credential harvesting, password spraying against Exchange and Microsoft 365 interfaces, SoftEther VPN persistence, DCSync and bulk mail theft through Exchange Web Services. Five of the eight old flaws the advisory lists as successfully exploited (ProFTPD, ISC BIND, Apache Struts, ONLYOFFICE Docs, Strapi) were added to CISA's KEV catalog the same day; the FBI also seized the domains behind MicroScan and the FishHub phishing tool.

records.title: CVE-2026-107406, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: a SAML-path memory overflow that can lead to code execution still affects the 2026-10-03 fixed builds on identity-provider appliances (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Citrix: a new NetScaler SAML overflow, rated Critical, reaches the builds that fixed the previous one
records.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697191 (2026-10-08, severity Critical) fixes CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway that leads to remote code execution or denial of service (CVSS 4.0 9.5) when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. An identity-provider appliance is affected through the 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 builds that Citrix named for CVE-2026-88779 and must move to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds; Citrix says it is not aware of any unmitigated exploits.
actions: Upgrade each SAML identity-provider NetScaler (`add authentication samlIdPProfile`) straight to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29, 14.1-73.46 FIPS or 13.1.37.283 (13.1-FIPS and NDcPP), including appliances already on 14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28; a service-provider-only appliance (`add authentication samlAction`) below 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 (FIPS and NDcPP: 13.1-37.279) needs the same builds.

records.title: BigDiskBuster: a roughly 300-line Windows proof of concept keeps Microsoft Defender from updating by claiming all free disk space, with no CVE and no patch
records.headline: A Defender bypass that needs no vulnerability: fill the disk during every update and the engine stays up, stale
records.summary: LevelBlue SpiderLabs reproduced BigDiskBuster, a proof of concept published on GitHub on 2026-09-19 by the actor known as MSNightmare, which watches the C: volume for Defender update activity and claims the free space so each update fails while the Defender service keeps running and real-time protection stays on. It runs from a standard account and has no CVE or patch; Microsoft says Defender Antivirus detects the proof of concept, and no use in attacks is reported.

records.title: A phishing link on Microsoft's own Power BI domain slips past mail filters and installs rogue ScreenConnect clients, then, in one incident, a script replaces the first remote-management tool with a second
records.headline: Huntress: a Power BI-hosted phishing link installs rogue ScreenConnect clients; in one case a script removed the first
records.summary: Huntress describes a phishing campaign seen since 2026-09-10 in which an Outlook email links to a fake reference document on a legitimate Power BI domain; a "Download Reference" button opens an attacker page that fingerprints the visitor and then downloads a ScreenConnect installer. The installer deploys a rogue ScreenConnect client that establishes a second one, and in one incident a PowerShell script removed the first; Huntress could not obtain the original email, and the configuration of one of the rogue clients also appeared on 22 other endpoints.

records.title: Ixa Systems, a Vaud security integrator serving police, prisons and banks: camera locations, plans and some passwords that TheGentlemen claimed to have stolen are reported on sale on the darknet
records.headline: Site plans, camera locations and some credentials of Vaud prisons and banks, and of police premises, reported for sale
records.summary: Le Temps reports, and the AWP news agency names the firm as Ixa Systems of Crissier (Vaud), that data stolen from a video-surveillance, alarm and access-control integrator is on sale on the darknet; the group TheGentlemen claimed the theft at the end of August. The loot reportedly includes camera locations, security-installation plans and, in some cases, usernames or passwords, for clients including police authorities, gendarmerie premises, prisons, hospitals, schools and banks; the reports do not state the access vector or list every affected site.
actions: If your organisation bought video-surveillance, alarm or access-control installation or maintenance from Ixa Systems, ask the firm in writing which of your sites and credentials are in the stolen data and rotate every camera, alarm, intercom and remote-maintenance credential it held.
